sixStepMethod.title: Extract hard constraints
sixStepMethod.what: Compliance, latency, data residency, RPO/RTO, budget ceilings, existing commitments. Separate them from preferences ("would like").

sixStepMethod.title: Separate requirements from assumptions
sixStepMethod.what: Write down anything you are assuming (traffic, team skills). Exam scenarios usually state what matters; do not import extra facts.

sixStepMethod.title: Generate candidates
sixStepMethod.what: Use the matrices: requirement -> candidate -> why it fits.

sixStepMethod.title: Eliminate with disqualifiers
sixStepMethod.what: For each candidate, check "When not to choose it". One violated hard constraint eliminates it.

sixStepMethod.title: Compare the nearest alternative
sixStepMethod.what: Name what the runner-up would do better; this is often the trap option.

sixStepMethod.title: Verify
sixStepMethod.what: List the fact you would check in documentation and the test that would prove the design works.

managedServicesPrinciple: Managed services are a conditional preference, not an exam law. Prefer a managed option when it satisfies every hard requirement and removes operational work your team does not need to own. Reject it when a constraint (protocol, OS access, data residency, licensing, cost at scale) rules it out. The same applies to "newest name" and "Google-native": choose them only when they meet the requirements.

conflicts.topic: CDL blueprint: PDF vs HTML guide
conflicts.conflict: PDF guide (footer 'launched on August 12, 2026'): 18/18/18/18/10. HTML guide page: 17/16/16/17/17 with older product names.
conflicts.handling: The certification page states the new exam version is live as of August 12, 2026 and links the PDF; this publication follows the PDF. If you sat or scheduled an exam governed by the older version, use the HTML weights.

conflicts.conflict: GKE Enterprise release notes say GKE is a single offering without editions or tiers; the CDL guide still lists 'GKE Enterprise' as a hybrid/multicloud product.
conflicts.handling: Recognise 'GKE Enterprise' and 'Anthos' as earlier names for GKE's fleet/multi-cluster capabilities; Anthos clusters are now Google Distributed Cloud. Treat as successor/rebrand, not a one-to-one rename.

conflicts.conflict: Beta: 3 h, ~80 items, US$120, English, results end of October, labs due 31 Dec 2026. GA exam announced for mid-November; GA logistics not yet published at retrieval.
conflicts.handling: All PAA logistics are flagged change-sensitive; re-check the page before registering.

conflicts.conflict: Product documentation states 'Looker Studio is now called Data Studio'; the ADP guide uses 'Looker Studio'.
conflicts.handling: Both names shown; expect guide wording on the exam until the guide is revised.

conflicts.conflict: Original stated 50 Mbps-50 Gbps; the range was not located in the retrieved overview page.

readinessRubric.caution: These are learning rubrics for self-assessment and mentoring. They are not Google scoring models and are not validated predictors of passing an exam. A strong quiz score does not offset a "Not yet demonstrated" in hands-on execution or troubleshooting; treat any such gap as open.

dimensions.meaning: Explains the concept, its purpose and its limits in your own words.
dimensions.evidence: Explanation without notes; correct limits stated (e.g. "a budget does not cap spend").

dimensions.meaning: Selects the best option and explains why each alternative fails.
dimensions.evidence: Error log with corrected rules; reasoning written for every option.

dimensions.meaning: Implements and verifies in a sandbox following current docs.
dimensions.evidence: Exercise evidence: commands, outputs, positive and negative tests.

dimensions.meaning: Diagnoses a fault from symptoms and restores service safely.
dimensions.evidence: Operate-table drills; timeline of diagnosis; rollback evidence.

dimensions.meaning: Chooses under conflicting constraints and documents trade-offs.
dimensions.evidence: ADR with eliminated options and verification plan.

dimensions.meaning: Explains a decision to the right audience with sources.
dimensions.evidence: Briefing or ADR reviewed by someone else; cited sources.
